identity.title: Editing of SpNRAMP3, SpCAX3, and SpHMA3 differentially affects cadmium concentrations and growth responses in Sedum plumbizincicola.

content.abstract: Sedum plumbizincicola is a Cd/Zn hyperaccumulator with exceptional Cd tolerance and shoot accumulation capacity. Here, bioinformatic analysis, subcellular localization, heterologous expression in yeast, and CRISPR/Cas9-mediated genome editing were combined to characterize the role of SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation and its functional relationships with SpCAX3 and SpHMA3. SpNRAMP3 encodes a protein with 11 predicted transmembrane domains and shows a localization pattern consistent with tonoplast association; it is expressed in roots, stems and leaves and displays Cd-responsive expression. Heterologous expression of SpNRAMP3 in yeast increased cellular Cd accumulation and conferred Cd hypersensitivity. Two independent SpNRAMP3-edited lines showed greater Cd sensitivity and lower Cd concentrations in young leaves, supporting a role for SpNRAMP3 in Cd homeostasis, growth response, and tissue Cd allocation. Heterologous expression of SpCAX3 also altered cellular Cd accumulation and Cd sensitivity in yeast. Compared with the wild type, the spnramp3spcax3 double-edited lines showed 72.5-79.8% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves and reduced relative growth inhibition under Cd stress, whereas the spnramp3sphma3 lines showed 28.2-58.6% lower Cd concentrations in young leaves but substantially greater growth inhibition. These results suggest that SpHMA3 primarily mediates vacuolar Cd sequestration, whereas SpNRAMP3 and SpCAX3 may contribute to Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation through distinct but functionally connected processes. These proteins may act together to support Cd hyperaccumulation and hypertolerance in S. plumbizincicola. This study provides a framework for understanding Cd homeostasis and tissue Cd allocation in hyperaccumulator plants and identifies candidate targets for genome-editing-based improvement of phytoremediation.
